reasons.not_site_wide: The link to {target, select, github {your GitHub} other {your Tela profile}} is on {page} but not on {other}, your blog's page for a missing address. Without rel="me", a link counts only if that page shows it too, in a header or footer, so a link in a post does not. Add rel="me" to it, or move it to your header or footer.
reasons.no_not_found_page: The link to {target, select, github {your GitHub} other {your Tela profile}} on {page} has no rel="me", so Tela looks for it on your blog's 404 page too, and your blog does not answer a missing address with a 404 page Tela can read. Add rel="me" to the link.
reasons.github_website: Your blog links to your GitHub profile, but the website on that profile is not {site}. Set it to {site} on GitHub, then verify again.
reasons.github_link: Your GitHub profile names {site} as its website, but {page} does not link to that profile. Add the link to your header or footer.
reasons.github_unavailable: GitHub did not answer, so Tela could not check your GitHub. Try again in a little while, or use another way.
reasons.overruled: An operator removed or turned down this claim, so a link without rel="me" no longer proves it. Add rel="me" to the link to {target, select, github {your GitHub} other {your Tela profile}} on {page}, or add the meta tag.
reasons.home_refused: {page} turned Tela away (HTTP {status}). Bot protection usually does this: Cloudflare, a firewall or a security plugin. Let requests whose user agent starts with “Tela/” through, then verify again.
reasons.home_status: {page} answered HTTP {status} rather than a page Tela could read. Check that your home page loads, then verify again.
reasons.home_unreachable: Tela could not read {page}: {why, select, timeout {it took too long to answer} too_large {the page is larger than Tela reads} redirect_loop {it redirects too many times} other {it could not be reached}}. Check that it loads, then verify again.

reading.title: How Tela reads your blog
reading.intro: Tela is a feed reader. It reads the RSS, Atom or JSON feed your blog already publishes, as any feed reader does, and asks your server for as little as it can.

agent.title: It says who it is
agent.body: Every request carries Tela’s user agent, Tela/0.1 (+https://telaread.com; feed reader), or for images Tela/0.1 (+https://telaread.com; image proxy).

often.title: About as often as you post
often.body: Tela checks your feed about twice as often as you published over the past week: every 30 minutes at most, and at least once a day. Each check that finds nothing new waits a little longer for the next. Your feed’s ttl and Cache-Control: max-age can ask it to wait longer, up to a day.

changed.title: Only what changed
changed.body: Each check sends back the ETag and Last-Modified your server gave, so a feed that hasn’t changed costs a 304 and nothing more.

errors.title: It backs off
errors.body: When your server fails or doesn’t answer, Tela waits twice as long after each failure, up to a week, and as long as a Retry-After asks. After a 410 Gone, or 30 failures in a row, it tries once a week.

images.title: Images when someone reads
images.body: The images in your posts are fetched only when someone reads the post, through Tela’s image proxy, and then kept for a week.

pages.title: Your pages, only when the feed is short
pages.body: If your feed carries only summaries, Tela fetches each new post’s public page once, soon after the feed lists it, to show the full text to subscribers in the reader, and again only if the summary changes. It reads your home page once, when your blog is added, to find its icon. Both ask your robots.txt first.

public.title: In public, titles and excerpts
public.body: Tela’s public pages, the ones anyone and any search engine can open, show your posts’ titles and short excerpts, each linking to the post on your blog. They never show a post in full.

members.title: To subscribers, your posts in full
members.body: Members who subscribe to your blog read your posts in full, in Tela’s reader and in the apps Tela approves, from your feed or the post’s page, as in any feed reader. Other members can open a limited number of posts a day from blogs they don’t follow, and visitors see only excerpts. If you turn translation off, Tela stops translating your blog and stops sending its translations to readers and apps.

translation.title: Translations, labelled
translation.body: Titles and excerpts are translated ahead of time into Tela’s reading languages, so readers can find your posts. A post itself is translated only for a reader who asks for it. Every translation is a machine’s, labelled as one and shown beside your original, and you can turn translation off for your blog.

claiming.title: Claiming your blog
claiming.intro: Claiming tells Tela the blog is yours. You need a Tela account and any one of these:

link.title: A link to your Tela profile
link.body: A link to telaread.com/@you on your home page marked rel="me", or without it, in a header or footer your 404 page shows too, so it is your blog’s own link and not a mention in a post.

meta.title: A meta tag
meta.body: The tela-site-verification tag Tela gives you, in your home page’s head. You can remove it once the claim is verified.

github.title: Your GitHub
github.body: Nothing to add, if you sign in with GitHub, your GitHub profile names your blog as its website, and your blog links to that profile in one of the ways above.

claiming.check: To check, Tela reads your home page and, for a link without rel="me", one address your blog doesn’t have, to see its 404 page.
claiming.gives: A claimed blog is listed in Discover under your name. Your Dashboard shows how many read it on Tela, which posts they liked and recommended, and the notes they left; there you choose its topics, whether it is translated, and whether Tela uses only your feed.

optOut.title: If you’d rather Tela didn’t
optOut.intro: Each of these holds as soon as it is made. The last two need no claim.

translation.title: Turn translation off
translation.body: On your Dashboard, once your blog is claimed. Readers then see your posts only as you wrote them.

feedOnly.title: Only use what my feed provides
feedOnly.body: Also on your Dashboard. Tela stops fetching your blog’s pages, for full text and for its icon, and reads only your feed. If your feed carries whole posts, subscribers still read them in full, as in any feed reader; if it carries summaries, they read those and follow the link to your blog.

robots.title: robots.txt
robots.body: To keep Tela off your pages without claiming anything, add this to your robots.txt. Tela reads it again within a day.
robots.after: As with any crawler, a group naming Tela takes the place of the one for everyone (User-agent: *). Your feed is still read, as every feed reader reads it: a subscriber asked for it.

email.title: Leave Tela
email.body: Write to <mail>me@hutu.si</mail>, and Tela will take your blog out of Discover, remove its page on Tela and stop fetching it. If you can’t claim the blog, the switches above can be set for you the same way.

settings.showLikesHint: On your profile, and to people who follow you. A writer's Dashboard shows how many liked a post, not who.
settings.showSubscriptionsHint: On your profile, and to people who follow you.
settings.privacyWaits: Turning this back on waits until your last change to it has reached Tela.
settings.privacyDelay: Your public profile can take a few minutes to catch up with a change.
settings.yourDataHint: Your profile, subscriptions, likes, recommendations, highlights and the people you follow, as one file.
settings.translationsHint: A post Tela has already translated, and a switch between the Chinese scripts, don’t count. The count starts again at {time}.
settings.translationsFree: No daily limit applies to your account.
settings.translationsWaiting: {n, plural, one {One translation waits} other {# translations wait}} to start after {time}.
settings.subscriptionsPending: {n, plural, one {One imported blog waits} other {# imported blogs wait}} to be added. invites.intro: Tela is invite-only for now. You can invite five people: a code lets one person in, and once used it counts for good. Revoke a code nobody has used to get its place back.
invites.open: Anyone can join Tela now, no invite code needed. Your codes are kept, and work again if Tela goes back to invitations.
invites.left: {n, plural, =0 {You have invited everyone you can.} one {You can invite # more person.} other {You can invite # more people.}}
invites.none: No codes yet. Create one, then send its link to a friend.

errors.allowance_used: You have invited five people already.
errors.rate_limited: Too many codes in an hour. Try again later.
errors.failed: That did not work. Try again.
errors.load: Your codes could not be loaded. Try again later.

account.intro: How you sign in to Tela. Each change is mailed to you, and adding a way to sign in signs out your other devices.
account.passwordSet: Set. You can still sign in with an emailed code.
account.passwordNone: Not set. You sign in with an emailed code.
account.everywhereHint: Ends every session on every device, this one included.
account.confirmHint: To change how you sign in, confirm it's you with a code sent to your email.
account.confirmSent: We sent a code to {email}. Enter it here.

errors.rejected: That was not accepted. Check the password and try again.
errors.rate_limited: Too many changes. Try again later.
errors.failed: That did not work. Try again.
errors.link_failed: That account could not be linked. Try again.
errors.load: Your sign-in methods could not be loaded. Try again later.

delete.label: Delete account
delete.hint: Removes your account and what you keep on Tela, for good.
delete.title: Delete your account?
delete.goes: Your name, bio, picture, notes and blogrolls disappear at once, and so do the people you follow and your followers. Every device is signed out. What you kept for yourself (subscriptions, folders, highlights, likes, what you read) is removed within minutes. Blogs you claimed are released, keeping the settings you chose for them.
delete.stays: Your handle {handle} is retired, so nobody can take it to pass as you. Tela’s backups keep a copy for 30 days, then it is gone.
delete.export: To keep a copy, <link>download your data</link> first.
delete.sent: We sent a code to {email}. Enter it to delete your account.

errors.admin: This account runs Tela’s admin console. Hand the console on first, then delete the account.
errors.bad_code: That code is not right, or it has expired. Ask for a new one.
errors.rate_limited: Too many tries. Try again later.
errors.failed: That did not work. Try again.

connectedApps.intro: Apps you have connected to your Tela account, and what each may do. Tela approves every app before anyone can connect it.
connectedApps.noneBody: Apps made by other developers can read your Tela and, if you let them, make changes for you, such as marking posts read. Tela approves each one before anyone can connect it, and you choose what it may do when you connect it from the app.
connectedApps.when: Connected {since} · {used} · {devices, plural, =0 {no devices} one {# device} other {# devices}}
connectedApps.confirm: Disconnect {name}? It stops working on all your devices at once. What it has already kept stays with it: ask the app to delete it.
connectedApps.more: <link>What apps can see</link>, and what Tela keeps about each connection.

errors.load: Your connected apps couldn’t be loaded. Try again later.
errors.failed: It couldn’t be disconnected. Try again.

developer.intro: Apps you register for Tela’s API: programs people connect to their Tela account, to read it or to act for them. <guide>How the API works</guide>
developer.noneBody: An app is a program, for you or for others, that connects to Tela accounts: a reader in the terminal, a phone app, a script. <guide>Read the API guide</guide> to make one.
developer.noneLimits: An app starts in Testing, where only you can connect it, and can go Live for everyone once it has a privacy policy. Until Tela reviews it, it can hold only a limited number of members, and can’t ask for their email addresses.
developer.rules: Every app is held to the <rules>developer rules</rules>, and you are responsible for yours.
developer.capNote: Apps Tela hasn’t reviewed share a cap: {cap} members connected at once, across all your unreviewed apps. Your own connection doesn’t count. A review lifts the cap.

statusBody.approved: Anyone on Tela can connect it.
statusBody.suspended: Tela has cut it off: it works for no one, and it can’t be changed or deleted.

developer.connections: {n, plural, one {# member} other {# members}} connected
developer.testingConfirm: Put {name} back in Testing? Everyone but you is disconnected from it at once, and only you can connect it until it goes Live again.
developer.deleteConfirm: Delete {name}? Everyone connected to it is disconnected at once, and its client ID stops working for good. This can’t be undone.
developer.reviewIntro: A review is optional. Tela looks at the app, its homepage and its privacy policy, and may write to its contact address. Once reviewed, the app is no longer held to the cap on members, and it may ask members for their email address.

form.title: A new app
form.name: Name
form.nameHint: What members see when they connect it. Only Tela’s own apps may use the word “Tela”.
form.developerHint: Who makes it: you, or your team. Until Tela reviews the app, members see your @handle instead.
form.contactHint: Where Tela writes to you about this app. Members never see it. Left empty, it is your account’s address.
form.urlHint: Both https, and both linked on the page where members connect the app. It can’t go Live without a privacy policy.
form.redirectHint: One a line, at most {n}: http://127.0.0.1/… or http://[::1]/… (any port matches), or the app’s own scheme, such as com.example.app:/callback. Never localhost.
form.maxScope: The most it may ask for
form.terms: I accept the <rules>developer rules</rules>, and I am responsible for this app and for what it does with members’ data.
form.clearsReview: Changing the name, the redirect URIs or the most it may ask for clears Tela’s review: until Tela reviews it again, the app is held to the cap on members and can’t see email addresses.

errors.name: Give it a name of up to {name} characters.
errors.nameTela: Only Tela’s own apps may use the word “Tela” in a name, so that no app is taken for Tela itself.
errors.developer: Say who makes it, in up to {text} characters.
errors.developerTela: Only Tela’s own apps may name Tela as their developer, so that no app is taken for Tela itself.
errors.contactEmail: A contact address must be one that receives mail.
errors.homepageUrl: The homepage must be an https address.
errors.privacyUrl: The privacy policy must be an https address.
errors.redirectUris: One to {n} redirect URIs, each different: a loopback address over http, or the app’s own reverse-DNS scheme. Never localhost, never https.
errors.maxScope: Choose the most it may ask for.
errors.terms: Accept the developer rules to register an app.

errors.load: Your apps couldn’t be loaded. Try again later.
errors.app_limit: One account may register {limit, plural, one {# app} other {# apps}}, and you have that many. Delete one to register another.
errors.rate_limited: You’ve registered or changed apps as often as one day allows. Try again later.
errors.privacy_required: Add a privacy policy first: the page where members connect the app links to it, so the app can’t go Live without one.
errors.cut_off: Tela has cut this app off, so it can’t be deleted.
errors.reported: Someone has reported this app, so it can’t be deleted until Tela has looked at the report.

connect.title: Connect an app

signIn.title: Connect an app to Tela
signIn.body: An app is asking to connect to your Tela account. Log in to see what it asks for. Nothing is shared until you say yes.

connect.draft: Not yet approved by Tela. Only you can connect it, because it is registered to your account for testing.
connect.heading: Connect {app} to your Tela account?

level.label: What it can do
level.readBody: See your subscriptions and folders, posts and their full text, your likes, recommendations and highlights, your reading history, the people you follow, your reading preferences, and public pages. It can’t change anything, or ask for translations.
level.writeBody: See all of that, and change it for you: mark posts read, like, recommend, highlight, subscribe, add feeds, file blogs in folders, follow people, change your reading preferences, and ask for translations, which count toward your daily translations.

connect.email: Let it see your email address

never.label: No app can
never.signIn: Change how you sign in, or your password
never.admin: Do anything only the person who runs Tela can

returns.loopback: When you answer, you go back to the app on this computer ({target}).
returns.scheme: When you answer, you go back to the app ({target}).

connect.responsibility: What {app} keeps is its own responsibility, under <policy>its privacy policy</policy>, not Tela’s.
connect.responsibilityNoPolicy: What {app} keeps is its own responsibility, not Tela’s. It has given Tela no privacy policy.
connect.later: You can disconnect it at any time in Settings → Connected apps. That stops it at once, but doesn’t delete what it has already kept. <link>More about apps</link>

sent.loopback: Your browser is going back to the app. If nothing happens, switch to the app yourself; you can close this page.
sent.scheme: Your browser is asking to open the app. If nothing happens, switch to the app yourself; you can close this page.

errors.title: This app can’t connect
errors.invalid_client: Tela doesn’t know this app. It may have been removed, or the link that brought you here is wrong.
errors.invalid_redirect: The app asked Tela to send you somewhere it never registered, so Tela won’t.
errors.invalid_request: The app’s request is incomplete or malformed. Try connecting again from the app.
errors.unsupported_response_type: The app asked to connect in a way Tela doesn’t offer.
errors.invalid_scope: The app asked for more than Tela lets it have.
errors.app_unavailable: This app can’t be connected now: it isn’t approved yet, or Tela has paused it.
errors.max_connections: This app has as many people connected as Tela allows for now. Try again later.
errors.failed: Check your connection and try again.
errors.nothingShared: Nothing was shared with the app.
errors.decideFailed: Your answer didn’t reach Tela. Try again.

search.noArticles: No posts in your subscriptions match.

report.intro: Your report goes to the person who runs Tela, and only to them. Nobody is told who sent it.
report.thanksBody: Your report is in. It will be read, and acted on if it needs to be.
